title: Parity of the Vertically Shifted Cosine Function f(x) = 1 + cos(x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the function f(x) = 1 + cos(x) is even, odd, or neither, and justify your answer.

steps.title: Evaluate f(-x)
steps.explanation: Replace x with -x in the expression 1 + cos(x).
steps.why: Testing for even or odd parity begins by computing f(-x).

steps.title: Simplify Using Cosine Symmetry
steps.explanation: Since cos(-x) = cos(x) for all real x, the expression simplifies directly to 1 + cos(x) = f(x).
steps.why: Both the constant function 1 and cos(x) are invariant under x -> -x.

steps.title: Conclude Function Parity
steps.explanation: Since f(-x) = f(x) for all x in R, f(x) = 1 + cos(x) is an even function.
steps.why: Shifting an even function vertically preserves its y-axis symmetry.
